I'm so glad I'm finally talking to someone. I've been feeling really overwhelmed since the baby was born. I just feel tired all the time, like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of her, but I don't really have the energy to enjoy it. And the worries, oh my goodness, the worries are constant. Is she eating enough? Is she safe? What if something happens to her? Sometimes I can calm myself down, but other times it's hard to stop thinking about all the things that could go wrong. I just feel so sad and discouraged a lot of the time, like I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom. And some nights, I just can't sleep because my mind is racing with all these anxious thoughts. I've even had some thoughts of...of not being able to handle it all, but I don't think I could ever actually do anything to hurt myself. I just feel so guilty and like I'm failing somehow. Does that sound crazy?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

To be honest, it's been a while since I've really laughed or felt like I can see the funny side of things. I mean, I'll watch a funny video or something and I'll smile, but it's not the same as really feeling carefree and laughing like I used to before the baby was born. Most of the time, I just feel so serious and worried about everything. Even when I'm doing things I used to enjoy, like reading or taking a walk, it's just not as enjoyable as it used to be. I feel like I'm just going through the motions a lot of the time. Sometimes I'll have a good moment with the baby, like when she smiles at me or something, and that brings me some joy, but it's fleeting. Mostly, I just feel anxious and overwhelmed, and it's hard for me to find the humor in things right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

That's something that's really changed for me since the baby was born. I used to look forward to all sorts of things, like going out with friends, trying new restaurants, or just relaxing on the weekends. But now, I don't really feel like I have the energy or the enthusiasm to look forward to things like I used to. Even things that I used to enjoy, like taking a bath or reading a book, just feel like chores now. I'll think about doing something I used to like, and I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the things I need to do to take care of the baby, and I'll end up not doing it at all. Sometimes I'll plan something, like a walk with a friend, and then the day of, I'll just feel too tired or anxious to follow through. It's hard to explain, but it's like the excitement and anticipation I used to feel about things has just been drained out of me. The only thing I really look forward to is maybe getting a few hours of sleep, or having some help with the baby so I can take a break. That sounds really sad, doesn't it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not sleeping, I think it's because I didn't establish a good routine. If she's not eating enough, I think it's because I'm not producing enough milk. It's like I'm always questioning my abilities as a mother and wondering what I'm doing wrong. Even when things are going well, I'll find a way to pick apart what I'm doing and think about how I could be doing it better. It's exhausting, to be honest. I feel like I'm always walking on eggshells, waiting for something to go wrong so I can beat myself up over it. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to burp her and she spits up, I'll think "Oh, I'm such a bad mom, I should have remembered to burp her." It's like I'm always looking for ways to criticize myself, and it's really hard to shake that feeling. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeling okay, and then I'll just start thinking about all the things I've done wrong and I'll start to feel guilty and anxious all over again. It's a really hard cycle to break.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been happening to me a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, just taking care of the baby, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something. Like, what if the house catches on fire? What if someone breaks in? What if the baby stops breathing? It's always something, and it's always something that's unlikely to happen, but it feels so real in the moment. And it's not just big things, it's little things too. Like, I'll be worried that I'm not making enough milk, or that the baby is not gaining enough weight. It's like my mind is always looking for something to worry about, and it's exhausting. Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll get this knot in my stomach and I'll feel like I'm going to be sick. It's hard to calm myself down, and sometimes it takes a while to realize that there's no real reason to be worried. But even when I do calm down, the worry is always lurking in the back of my mind, just waiting to pounce again. It's like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll worry about my relationship with my partner, or about how I'm going to get everything done, or about what other people think of me as a mom. It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that I don't know how to shake.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to be sick. It's like my body is reacting to something, but my mind can't figure out what it is. It's really scary, because I feel like I'm losing control. Sometimes it's triggered by something small, like a loud noise or a unexpected movement, but other times it just seems to come out of nowhere. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear. It's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll feel like I'm not safe, like something is going to happen to me or to the people I love. It's hard to explain, because it doesn't make sense, even to me. But it's like my body is responding to some kind of threat, even when there isn't one. And it's hard to calm down, because my mind is racing and I feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. Sometimes I'll try to take some deep breaths, or go for a walk, or do something to distract myself, but it's hard to shake the feeling of panic once it's started. It's like I'm stuck in this cycle of fear, and I don't know how to get out of it.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I feel. Like everything is just piling up on me and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a full-time job, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm constantly running on a treadmill and getting nowhere. I'll get one thing done, and then something else will come up, and I'll feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. And it's not just the physical tasks, it's the emotional ones too. I feel like I'm constantly worrying about the baby, and about being a good mom, and about everything else in my life. It's like I'm shouldering this huge burden, and I don't know how to put it down. Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a functioning person, but really I'm just barely holding it together. I'll put on a brave face and go through the motions, but inside I'm feeling completely overwhelmed. And it's hard to ask for help, because I feel like I should be able to do it all on my own. But the truth is, I don't know how much more of this I can take. Some days, I just feel like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me for a while now. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when she's sleeping, I'll lie awake for hours, just feeling unhappy and anxious. My mind will start racing, and I'll think about all the things that are worrying me, and I'll feel this heaviness in my chest. It's like I'm carrying around this weight of sadness and responsibility, and it's just exhausting. Sometimes I'll fall asleep for a little while, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like I'm grieving for the person I used to be, before I had the baby. I know that sounds silly, but it's true. I feel like I've lost myself in all of this, and I don't know how to find my way back. And the lack of sleep just makes everything worse. I'll be tired and irritable, and I'll feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby, rather than actually being present with her. It's hard to enjoy the moments with her when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and unhappy. Sometimes I'll have a good day, and I'll think, "Okay, maybe I'm turning a corner," but then the next day will come, and I'll feel just as bad as before. It's like I'm stuck in this cycle of sadness and anxiety, and I don't know how to break free.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been my reality for a while now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling anything positive. I'll have moments where I'll smile or laugh, but it's not the same as really feeling happy or fulfilled. Most of the time, I just feel sad and miserable. I'll be taking care of the baby, and I'll think about how I'm supposed to be enjoying this time, but I'm not. I'll think about how I'm supposed to be feeling grateful and blessed, but I'm not. I just feel overwhelmed and anxious, and like I'm not doing anything right. Sometimes I'll look at other moms, and I'll think they have it all together, and I'll feel even more miserable because I don't feel like I do. I'll feel like I'm failing as a mom, and that's a really hard feeling to shake. Even when the baby is being cute or doing something new, I'll feel a pang of sadness because I'm not feeling the joy that I think I should be feeling. It's like I'm observing my life from the outside, rather than actually living it. And it's hard to explain to people, because they'll say things like, "Oh, you're just tired," or "You're just adjusting to motherhood," but it's more than that. It's like I'm lost and alone, and I don't know how to find my way back to myself. Sometimes I'll cry, just because I feel so sad and overwhelmed, and it's like my body is just releasing all of this pent-up emotion. But even the crying doesn't really bring me any relief, because I'll just feel guilty for feeling sad, and I'll think about how I should be grateful for what I have. It's a really hard cycle to break, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the tears just come out of nowhere, and I don't even know why I'm crying half the time. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's not even like I'm thinking about anything sad, it's just like my emotions are so raw and close to the surface that anything can set me off. Sometimes it's just the exhaustion, or the feeling of being overwhelmed, and sometimes it's just the sadness and the feeling of being lost. I'll cry because I'm feeling guilty about something, or because I'm worried about the baby, or because I just feel like I'm not doing enough. And it's not just a little cry, either. I mean, I'll have full-on sobbing fits, where I'm crying so hard I can barely breathe. It's embarrassing, because sometimes my partner will be there, or my family will be visiting, and I'll just lose it in front of them. But at the same time, it's like my body is just releasing all of this tension and emotion, and it's the only way I can really express how I'm feeling. Sometimes I'll try to hold it in, because I don't want to burden anyone else with my emotions, but it's hard to keep it all inside. And when I do cry, it's like a weight is lifted off my shoulders, at least for a little while. But then the guilt sets in, and I'll think about how I should be stronger, or how I should be able to handle this, and it just starts the cycle all over again. It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just so emotionally raw and sensitive right now, and everything just feels like too much to handle.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

.. (pausing, looking down, and speaking in a barely audible whisper) Yes... I've had those thoughts. They're not something I'm proud of, and they scare me, but they're there. It's like, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and sad, and I don't know how to make it stop, my mind will start to wander to some really dark places. I'll think about how I just want to escape, or how I don't want to be a burden to anyone else, or how I just want to disappear. And sometimes, those thoughts will take a turn, and I'll think about harming myself. It's not something I want to do, and it's not something I think I would ever actually do, but the thoughts are there, and they're terrifying. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I know it sounds crazy, but it's like my mind is just trying to find a way out of the pain, and it's grasping at anything, even if it's something that's not healthy or safe. (looking up, with tears in my eyes) I don't know how to make it stop, or how to make the thoughts go away. I just know that I need help, and I need someone to talk to. (pausing, and speaking in a barely audible whisper) I'm so scared of those thoughts, and I'm so scared of what might happen if I don't get help.
